messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a staged encapsulation of the runtime <-> sidecar boundary to pay down a few long-standing debt items. Goal: extract session-affinity and the hot KV caching path into a small, well-tested sidecar with a stable, narrow API. Thinking of a three-phase approach: spike + contract, read-path migration, write-path migration + canary. Open for tradeoffs and constraints.

kevin: +1 to phased. Biggest tradeoff is the extra network hop; need concrete p50/p99 budget. Also want a fallback to in-process path for thin-tenants. Can we do a local loopback shim in spike to estimate overhead?

anna: Suggest a 2-day spike to build a shim sidecar that proxies calls to the runtime (no logic change) to measure latency and CPU scheduling noise. We'll also wire up a contract test harness that runs against the shim.

sam: Rollout concerns: canary by tenant cohort, automatic fallback to in-process if p99 exceeds threshold, circuit-breaker and exponential backoff at the client, and a break-glass override for emergent rollbacks. We should also include a safety window for cache warmup.

diego: Security notes: sidecar will need scoped access to tenant data (KMS keys/ACLs). We need an auth handshake and clear telemetry on auth failures. Also validate the sidecar runs in the same trust domain as runtime or has minimal privileges.

maria: Those are all good. Proposed timeline: spike (2w, incl perf + contract harness), implementation (6w), canary & rollouts (2w), observability & cost comparison (ongoing). Primary success criteria: p50 within +5ms of baseline, p99 within +20ms, no regression in unit-cost beyond 5% after batching tweaks.

anna: Add: include traces and token-level cost attribution so we can compare unit economics before/after. I'll add a perf dashboard query set.

infra-bot: Deploy bot: created canary cluster canary-encap-01 for early validation.

kevin: Cache consistency question — do we aim for strong consistency or optimized eventual consistency? My proposal: default to eventual with TTL and background reconciliation, but support strong consistency for a very small hot-key set (via a pinning API). I'll draft a short design doc.

maria: Action items: anna -> run spike and provide perf numbers; kevin -> cache consistency options doc; sam -> canary & rollback playbook; diego -> security requirements and KMS mapping. I'll open the follow-up RFC with the contract + perf targets and link it here. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll start the spike next Monday.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll sketch the canary checklist in this thread (tenant cohorts, thresholds, telemetry to compare before/after).

anna: Starting today — estimate 3 days for shim + basic bench harness, will post results here.

maria: Thanks everyone. One more constraint to keep in mind: runtime pins model versions and expects low-latency KV lookups for prefix caching. The API must support a fast 'get_many' path and a bounded async prefetch mechanism. Example contract sketch:

```
POST /sidecar/cache/get_many
headers: { x-tenant-id }
body: { keys: ["k1","k2",...], max_staleness_ms: 50 }
response: { values: [{ key: "k1", value: "...", ts: 171234 }], served_from: "memory|sidecar-db|fallback" }
```

maria: We'll keep the contract deliberately small to avoid long-lived coupling. Ping me if any blockers.

kevin: I'll drop a short doc on cache-ownership patterns and a recommended compatibility shim for old runtime callers.

diego: I'll enumerate the KMS & ACL changes, plus a minimal threat model.

maria: Will link RFC & tracking PRs here once created. If anything unexpected pops up please flag on #eng-oncall.

sam: Noted — will align SRE for the canary.

anna: Posting initial numbers tomorrow.

maria: Thanks — rolling forward unless objections.
